questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a helping verb (been) is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive. The preposition 'by' is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice sentence is given in interrogative form of present perfect tense. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in present perfect tense.

The format of Active voice is: Has/have + subject+ third form of verb + object?

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Has/Have + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)?

For example:

Active: Has she written a book?

Passive: Has a book been written by her?

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in superlative degree of comparison. She is less confident than her friends.

questions.solution:
The adjective is 'confident' and it is in the comparative degree, which means it compares one thing or person with another and shows that it has a higher or lower degree of quality. To change a sentence from the comparative degree to the superlative degree, we need to use 'least' before an adjective and use the word 'the' before it. The superlative degree shows that something or someone has the lowest degree of quality among all the others in a group.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is in positive degree.

Option (b) is in comparative degree.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.question: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. She couldn't resist the tempting bargain, a beautiful dress at half the price, (make her day) brighter and her wallet happier.

questions.solution:
In this sentence, the phrase "make her day brighter" should be in the present participle form to describe the concurrent action with the main clause. Option (b) is the correct choice. It uses the present participle "making," which fits the context and describes the concurrent action of the beautiful dress making her day brighter.

The rest of the options are grammatically incorrect.

'Is' needs to be followed by either past participle (V3) or present participle (-ing form of the verb), but 'make' is a base verb.

'Had' needs to be followed by the past participle (V3), but 'making' is the -ing form of the verb.

'Was made' [action directed towards the subject which isn't the correct case] fails to make the sentence meaningful.

The corrected sentence: She couldn't resist the tempting bargain, a beautiful dress at half the price, making her day brighter and her wallet happier.

Note:

A participle is a verbal, or a word based off of a verb that expresses a state of being, ending in -ing (present tense) or -ed, -en, -d, -t, -n, or -ne (past tense) that functions as an adjective. This means it needs to modify (or describe) a noun or a pronoun.

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['being' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

The cache memory is a very high speed and expensive memory, which is used to speed up the memory retrieval process. Due to its higher cost, the CPU comes with a smaller size of cache memory compared with the size of the main memory.

Without cache memory, every time the CPU requests the data, it has to be fetched from the main memory which will consume more time.

The idea of introducing a cache is that this extremely fast memory would store data that is frequently accessed and if possible, the data that is closer to it.

This helps to achieve the fast response time, Where response Time, (Access Time) refers to how quickly the memory can respond to a read / write request.

While they are high-speed, they are not typically referred to as "memory" in the context of speeding up memory retrieval, and they are not expensive in the same sense as cache.

c) RAM: Random Access Memory (RAM) is the main memory in a computer, used to store data and programs that the CPU needs to access. While RAM is faster than secondary storage (like a hard drive), it is much slower than cache memory and is not as expensive per byte as cache.

d) DVD: A DVD (Digital Versatile Disc) is a type of optical storage used for long-term data storage, not for speeding up memory retrieval. It is slow compared to cache, RAM, or even hard drives, and is irrelevant in this context.

Cache memory operates on the principle of locality (spatial and temporal), meaning it stores data that the CPU is likely to need soon, reducing access time significantly. It is more expensive per byte than RAM due to its speed and proximity to the CPU, and it typically comes in levels (L1, L2, L3) with varying sizes and speeds.

In Excel, a column range is written as "ColumnLetter:ColumnLetter" (e.g., A6:A18), where the column letter remains the same, and the row numbers define the range. A row range, on the other hand, changes the column letters (e.g., A1:D1).

When a CPU executes multiple programs simultaneously, the process is called multitasking. Multitasking allows a single CPU to switch between multiple tasks or programs rapidly, giving the appearance of simultaneous execution. This is typically managed by the operating system, which allocates CPU time to different processes or threads, ensuring that each program gets a fair share of processing resources.

Explanation of the Options:

b) Multiprocessing: This is incorrect in this context. Multiprocessing involves the use of multiple CPUs or CPU cores to execute different programs or tasks simultaneously. The question specifies a single CPU ("If CPU executes..."), so multiprocessing does not apply here.

c) Multiprogramming: While related, this is not the most precise term. Multiprogramming refers to keeping multiple programs in memory at the same time, allowing the CPU to switch between them when one program is waiting (e.g., for I/O operations). Multitasking is a broader and more commonly used term for the simultaneous execution scenario described.

d) Time-Sharing: This is a specific type of multitasking where CPU time is divided into small time slices, and each user or task gets a turn in a round-robin fashion. While time-sharing is a mechanism that enables multitasking, the general term for the CPU executing multiple programs simultaneously is "multitasking."

When you delete an email in most email clients or services (such as Gmail, Outlook, or Yahoo Mail), it is not permanently removed immediately. Instead, it is moved to a designated folder where it can be recovered if needed. This folder is typically called the Trash or Deleted Items folder, depending on the email service. The email remains in the Trash until it is either manually deleted from there or automatically purged after a set period (e.g., 30 days in Gmail).

Explanation of the Options:

a) Recycle Bin: This is incorrect. The Recycle Bin is a feature in operating systems like Windows for storing deleted files from the computer's file system (e.g., documents, photos), not for emails in an email client.

c) Spam: This is incorrect. The Spam folder is used to store emails flagged as unwanted or junk, not emails that the user has deleted.

d) Recent Files: This is incorrect. "Recent Files" is not a standard folder in email clients; it might refer to a feature in operating systems or applications for tracking recently accessed files, but it is unrelated to email deletion.

• Bridge is a network device that connects a local area network to another local area network that uses the same protocol.

• Gateway is a network node that connects two dissimilar networks using different protocols together.

• Repeater is an electronic device that magnifies the signal it receives. It is implemented in computer networks to expand the coverage area of the network. It is also known as signal boosters.

• Hub is a networking device which connects multiple network hosts. It is used to transfer data.

· Simplex Mode: In this type, the data can be transferred in only one direction. The only one can transmit and the other can receive the data. Example - Keyboard (Input) and Monitor (output), Loud Speaker, Television, Fire alarm system etc.

· Half Duplex Mode: In this type, the data can be transferred in both directions, but not at the same time. Example - Walkie-talkie.

· Full Duplex Mode: In this type, the data can be transferred in both direction on the same transmission path. Two lines are used for sending and receiving the data. Example - Telephone network.
